deployment_delay_drivers: Objective acceptance and commissioning criteria remain open.
The site-safety responsibility matrix is unsigned.
Connected-product data and remote-access controls require evidence.

signing_gate.review_gate: A named General Counsel and accountable Finance, Product, Safety, Security, and Commercial owners must approve consequential positions.

clause_reviews.issue: Acceptance depends on the customer's subjective satisfaction.
clause_reviews.requested_position: customer subjective acceptance after continuous production performance
clause_reviews.standard_position: Use objective site acceptance tests, measurable criteria, a fixed test window, a cure process, and deemed acceptance for operational use.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Permit one documented retest cycle against agreed criteria before deemed acceptance.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Acceptance can be delayed without objective failure criteria.
clause_reviews.rationale: Subjective acceptance can delay deployment, billing, and Finance's assessment of transfer of control.

clause_reviews.issue: The proposed data clause permits unrestricted telemetry and model-training use.
clause_reviews.requested_position: provider may use all data without restriction for any model training
clause_reviews.standard_position: Define product-data categories, user access, permitted service purposes, retention, security, trade-secret controls, and separate rules for model improvement.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Use aggregated or de-identified operational data for reliability improvement, subject to documented exclusions and customer access rights.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Training use involving personal data, confidential production data, or undefined purposes.
clause_reviews.rationale: Connected-product data, confidential manufacturing information, privacy, and model improvement require distinct legal and technical treatment.

clause_reviews.issue: The customer requests broad global industry exclusivity.
clause_reviews.requested_position: global industry-wide exclusivity for automotive components
clause_reviews.standard_position: No customer exclusivity over the provider's modular robotics platform or roadmap.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Consider a narrow, paid, time-limited site or use-case restriction with named competitors and minimum commercial commitments.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Any restriction affecting sales outside the named deployment and use case.
clause_reviews.rationale: Broad exclusivity can constrain a platform business beyond the value of one deal.

clause_reviews.issue: The customer claims ownership of site-specific and platform improvements.
clause_reviews.requested_position: customer owns all site-specific developments and improvements
clause_reviews.standard_position: The provider retains platform, robot, software, model, workflow, and generalised improvement IP. The customer retains its pre-existing IP and receives agreed use rights.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Grant a site-use licence for customer-funded deliverables while preserving provider ownership of reusable technology and de-identified know-how.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Any assignment of core technology, model behaviour, or reusable improvements.
clause_reviews.rationale: Overbroad ownership language can impair the product roadmap and create conflicting rights across deployments.

clause_reviews.issue: The customer requests uncapped liability across broad claim categories.
clause_reviews.requested_position: uncapped for indemnities, data, confidentiality, delay, and production loss
clause_reviews.standard_position: Use an aggregate cap linked to fees under the affected order form, with narrow exclusions supported by insurance and applicable law.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Offer a separately capped super-cap for defined privacy, security, confidentiality, or IP claims after Finance, Insurance, and General Counsel review.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Any uncapped exposure or cap above the approved authority matrix.
clause_reviews.rationale: Hardware, software, remote services, and physical operations can create exposure disproportionate to recurring fees.

clause_reviews.issue: Robot, integration, and customer site-safety responsibilities remain undocumented.
clause_reviews.requested_position: shared responsibilities to be agreed after signing and currently undocumented
clause_reviews.standard_position: Allocate machinery conformity, integration, guarding, site preparation, risk assessment, operating instructions, training, change control, and incident duties.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Use a signed responsibility matrix and site acceptance protocol before commissioning.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Deployment or production use before the signed safety responsibility matrix.
clause_reviews.rationale: A modular robot deployment crosses product design, system integration, customer-site controls, and operational change management.

clause_reviews.issue: The role of AI vision and path planning in safety functions remains open.
clause_reviews.requested_position: Product classification has not been finalised.
clause_reviews.standard_position: Document intended purpose, safety functions, failure effects, conformity path, human oversight, validation, change control, and technical-file ownership.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Block safety-relevant autonomous behaviour until accountable technical owners approve the classification and evidence set.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Any safety-relevant AI function is deployed without a recorded classification decision.
clause_reviews.rationale: The regulatory path depends on intended use, safety-component status, and the applicable conformity-assessment route.

clause_reviews.issue: The proposed incident-notification period may not support contractual or regulatory escalation.
clause_reviews.standard_position: Require prompt internal escalation and a contract notice window aligned with incident severity, legal duties, and verified information.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Use an initial material-incident notice followed by staged factual updates.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Remote access or product incident without an approved response and notification workflow.
clause_reviews.rationale: Remote maintenance and products with digital elements require coordinated security, privacy, product, and customer communications.

clause_reviews.issue: Service credits are uncapped and can accumulate outside the liability structure.
clause_reviews.requested_position: uncapped credits plus all other remedies
clause_reviews.standard_position: Use tiered service credits with a monthly cap, defined exclusions, measurement rules, and an agreed relationship to other remedies.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Increase the monthly credit cap for repeated failures while preserving an aggregate contractual ceiling.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Credits exceed the approved percentage of monthly RaaS fees.
clause_reviews.rationale: Uptime remedies affect variable consideration, margin, operational capacity, and wider liability exposure.

clause_reviews.issue: The customer can terminate for convenience without recovery of deployment costs.
clause_reviews.standard_position: Protect committed hardware, integration, installation, removal, and minimum-term costs.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Use a declining early-termination schedule tied to unrecovered deployment costs.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: Termination rights undermine the approved deal margin or contract term.
clause_reviews.rationale: RaaS economics depend on recovering hardware and deployment investment over time.

clause_reviews.issue: The provider retains title while risk of loss shifts to the customer after delivery.
clause_reviews.standard_position: Align title, custody, insurance, maintenance access, damage responsibility, and removal rights across the RaaS term.
clause_reviews.fallback_position: Customer bears site-custody risk after installation, subject to provider maintenance obligations and agreed insurance evidence.
clause_reviews.escalation_trigger: The insurance position does not match the title and custody allocation.
clause_reviews.rationale: Retained-title equipment requires a coherent allocation of custody, insurance, damage, access, and end-of-term recovery.

source_manifest.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854, Data Act
source_manifest.timing: Generally applies from 12 September 2025. Article 3(1) applies to connected products and related services placed on the market after 12 September 2026.

source_manifest.title: Directive 2006/42/EC, Machinery Directive
source_manifest.timing: Current EU machinery framework during the synthetic 2026 review, implemented through national law.

source_manifest.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Artificial Intelligence Act
source_manifest.timing: Generally applies from 2 August 2026. Article 6(1) and the corresponding product-linked high-risk obligations apply from 2 August 2027. Earlier phases under Article 113 must be checked separately.

source_manifest.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, Cyber Resilience Act
source_manifest.timing: Chapter IV applies from 11 June 2026. Article 14 applies from 11 September 2026. The Regulation generally applies from 11 December 2027.

source_manifest.title: Directive (EU) 2024/2853, Product Liability Directive
source_manifest.timing: Member States must transpose the Directive by 9 December 2026. The resulting national rules apply to products placed on the market or put into service after 9 December 2026.

source_manifest.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, General Data Protection Regulation
source_manifest.timing: In force and directly applicable. The concrete obligations depend on the roles, data, purposes, and transfer path.
